subject: MAP draft: Technical evaluation plan & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aria Sullivan <aria@hypernova.ai>, James Kim <james.kim@hypernova.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft: Technical evaluation plan & next steps

Hi Aria / James —

Great talking with you earlier. Thanks for walking us through HyperNova's priority use cases (customer support summarization + in-product recommendations). Per our call, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that scopes milestones, owners, and target dates. I highlighted the Technical Evaluation milestone since you asked for a concrete benchmark plan you can share with the engineering team.

Summary / immediate asks:
- Goal: Complete technical evaluation and decision to pilot by April 16, 2026.
- MAP attached: 20260302-HyperNova-MAP-draft.pdf (high level milestones + responsibilities).
- Benchmark plan (CSV attached) contains test harness details and initial eval set.

Technical evaluation (milestone: "Benchmark & Latency/Cost Gates") — draft items:
1) Success criteria (quality + safety):
   - Generation quality: pass rate >= 85% on 500-threaded customer-support prompts (human-rated F1/relevance).
   - Safety/PII: zero critical PII leak incidents on the eval set; documented redaction strategy required.
2) Latency targets (p95):
   - Interactive UI flows (512 tokens): p95 <= 350 ms for production-like traffic on Dedicated capacity (GPU A100 equivalent).
   - Batch inference (2k tokens): average latency <= 2s (for nightly batch jobs).
3) Cost targets (approx):
   - Target per-1000-token inference cost: <= $0.60 (hosted) / <= $0.25 (dedicated, after batching/quantization).
   - Target total pilot monthly compute cost: <= $6k.
4) Model shortlist to evaluate (initial):
   - Llama-3-13B (int8 quantized) — best mix of latency/quality for mid-sized models.
   - Mistral-7B-Instruct — low latency, lower cost candidate for lower-compute paths.
   - Falcon-40B-Instruct (quantized) — higher quality baseline to measure lift.
5) Evaluation harness & data:
   - We'll run the supplied eval set (see attached CSV) and a live shadow test for 48 hours on sample traffic.
   - Redwood will provide a test endpoint and a reproducible evaluation script.
6) Responsibilities / owners (draft):
   - HyperNova: provide labeled eval set + access to representative request logs (by 2026-03-09). Owner: Aria / James.
   - Redwood SEs: provision test endpoints, run benchmarks, and deliver latency/cost report (by 2026-03-20). Owner: Vivek.
   - Procurement/Legal: finalize SOW / NDA for pilot (target signature 2026-03-16). Owner: James / HyperNova procurement.

Dependencies: NDA signed, access to sample traffic that mirrors production, and confirmation whether a Dedicated pool is required for the pilot.

Next steps / propose schedule:
- By 2026-03-05: HyperNova shares eval set + any redaction constraints.
- By 2026-03-09: Redwood provides test endpoints and runbook for the benchmark.
- Benchmark run window: 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-19.
- Decision to pilot by 2026-04-16.

Please let me know if any of the targets above are unrealistic for you (especially the latency/cost targets) and we can adjust. I've cc'd Vivek (SE) and Michael (AE) to keep technical and commercial context on the thread.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 20260302-HyperNova-MAP-draft.pdf
Attachment: hypernova-benchmark-test-plan.csv

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Aria Sullivan <aria@hypernova.ai>, James Kim <james.kim@hypernova.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 18:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft: Technical evaluation plan & next steps

Marissa / Aria — quick SE notes on the draft technical evaluation plan. I pasted a short checklist for clarity.

Checklist / recommendations:
- Latency targets: can tighten interactive p95 to 250–300 ms for 256-token common paths if HyperNova can accept Llama-3-13B int8 as the primary candidate. For 512 tokens p95 ~350 ms is reasonable on dedicated A100 or H100-class nodes with batching disabled for interactive flows.
- Cost targets: our internal benchmark shows the following ballpark (after quantization + batching):
   * Llama-3-13B int8: ~$0.12 / 1k tokens on Dedicated pooled capacity.
   * Mistral-7B: ~$0.06 / 1k tokens.
   * Falcon-40B quantized: ~$0.40 / 1k tokens.
  I recommend we keep a flexible pilot budget but track per-model cost during runs.
- Model shortlist prioritization: run Mistral-7B first for latency/cost parity, Llama-3-13B for quality vs latency tradeoff, and Falcon-40B as a high-quality baseline.
- Eval harness: Redwood will provide a reproducible script + container. Please confirm whether HyperNova wants us to run a blind human evaluation or share outputs for your internal raters.

Technical dependencies we need from HyperNova:
1) Sample of typical request payloads (JSON) and distribution of sequence lengths.
2) Any custom transformers/prompts or prompt templates currently used.
3) Shadow-production endpoint IP allowlist or test tokens for hitting sample traffic.

Links:
- Draft MAP folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HyperNovaMAP
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

I'll slot time next week for a quick run-through of the evaluation harness. If you want the full microbench numbers (throughput / p95 / mem), I can attach after the first test run (ETA ~ 24–48 hours after we get the eval set).

—Vivek
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Aria Sullivan <aria@hypernova.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: James Kim <james.kim@hypernova.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft: Technical evaluation plan & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and concrete, appreciate the clarity. A few clarifying Qs from the engineering and procurement side:

1) Latency: our primary UI path typically averages ~300 tokens; p95 <= 350ms is realistic but we'd prefer to target p95 <= 300ms if possible. Could you confirm whether the 250–300ms p95 you mentioned for 256 tokens translates to ~300ms at 300 tokens in practice?

2) Cost: procurement is asking for an estimated TCO for the pilot (compute + storage + support). Is the ~$6k pilot monthly compute target accounting for Dedicated pool reservation, or is that just hosted usage? We may need a clearer split.

3) Timeline: best-case for us to share the eval set and representative logs is EOD 2026-03-05. Procurement can aim to have an SOW draft by 2026-03-12 but will need a short SOW template from Michael to speed review.

If those answers look OK, we'll proceed to sign the standard NDA first thing tomorrow and share the sample data.

Aria Sullivan
Head of ML Engineering
HyperNova Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aria Sullivan <aria@hypernova.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft: Technical evaluation plan & next steps

Aria — great questions, quick replies below and I updated the MAP (attached) to reflect Vivek's notes and your timeline.

1) Latency: yes — the 250–300ms p95 for 256 tokens generally maps to ~300–350ms for 300 tokens depending on batch/queueing behavior. We'll run the specific 300-token distribution you provide during the benchmark and report exact p95 numbers. Vivek will flag any infra adjustments (smaller batch sizes, dedicated instances) needed to hit p95 <= 300ms.

2) Cost: the $6k/month is a rough hosted estimate for the pilot window. For Dedicated reserved capacity we usually produce a separate estimate (monthly commit + expected overage). Michael, can you please share a short SOW template and an initial Dedicated vs Hosted cost sketch for HyperNova?

3) Timeline / next steps:
   - HyperNova: sign NDA & share eval set + logs by EOD 2026-03-05 (Aria/James).
   - Redwood: provide test endpoints + runbook by 2026-03-09 (Vivek).
   - Redwood: run benchmarks 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-19; deliver report 2026-03-20.

I'll attach the updated MAP reflecting these clarifications and the highlighted Technical Evaluation milestone. If HyperNova is aligned, we'll move NDA/signature tomorrow and I will set calendar invites for the test-run kickoffs.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: 20260302-HyperNova-MAP-draft.pdf (updated)
